This article compares the 30-day mortality rates among operated patients with a Charlson Score of 0—indicating no underlying comorbidities—across [[danmark|Danmark]]'s regions and hospitals. In the most recent reporting period, every region and hospital achieved a reported mortality proportion of 0%, meaning zero deaths occurred within this specific low-risk cohort [^src1]. However, because the absolute number of events is zero, the 95% confidence intervals (CI) highlight significant statistical uncertainty driven by small patient volumes [^src1].

While the current period shows uniform success, historical data from 2023/24 and 2022/23 reveals that mortality was previously present across the country. Nationally, the mortality rate dropped from 6.5% in 2022/23 to 6.1% in 2023/24 before reaching 0% in the current period [^src1]. Regionally, [[hovedstaden-region-i-alt|Hovedstaden Region i alt]] and [[nordjylland-region-i-alt|Nordjylland Region i alt]] historically recorded some of the higher rates, such as 8.5% and 8.0% respectively in the previous periods [^src1].

Several hospitals stand out as historical outliers or exhibit extreme statistical uncertainty in the current period. [[rigshospitalet|Rigshospitalet]] is a notable outlier: with only 9 patients in the current cohort, its 95% CI upper bound reaches 70.1%, and it previously recorded a 30.0% mortality rate in 2022/23 [^src1]. Similarly, [[bornholms-hospital|Bornholms Hospital]] shows extreme uncertainty with a CI upper bound of 52.7% despite zero current deaths [^src1]. In contrast, [[sygehus-lillebaelt|Sygehus Lillebælt]] reported zero deaths out of a larger cohort of 43 patients, yielding a much tighter CI upper bound of 8.2% [^src1].

Looking at historical leaders in mortality, [[esbjerg-sygehus-grindsted-sygehus|Esbjerg Sygehus Grindsted Sygehus]] reported a 14.3% mortality rate in 2023/24, while [[holbaek-sygehus|Holbæk Sygehus]] and [[regionshospitalet-horsens|Regionshospitalet Horsens]] recorded 13.3% and 12.2% respectively in 2022/23 [^src1]. The transition to 0% across all facilities in the current period represents a significant improvement for these previously high-mortality hospitals, though the wide confidence intervals at smaller institutions caution against assuming absolute zero risk [^src1].
